# Commands

Dispatch tasks to CLI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) in tmux windows and git worktrees. The same text is what `agentctl --help` and `agentctl <command> --help` print.

Options of every command: `-h, --help`. Options of `agentctl` itself: `-V, --version`.
Task IDs are case-insensitive and a unique prefix is enough for `attach`, `peek`, `hide`, `unhide`; the other commands take the full ID.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`version`](#agentctl-version) | Print the installed version (alias of --version). |
| [`guide`](#agentctl-guide) | Read the dispatcher guide and optional project overlay. |
| [`capacity`](#agentctl-capacity) | Current plan windows, pace, slots, queue, equivalents and seven-day model statistics; no provider selection. |
| [`hosts`](#agentctl-hosts) | Remote hosts over SSH (config section "hosts"): reachability, latency, GPU, disk in work_dir, tmux, provider CLIs (+ version, best-effort logged-in) and repo clones. Probes in parallel with a per-host timeout and caches the result for the board; a spec with "host: \<name>" starts its worktree, setup and agent there. |
| [`hosts add`](#agentctl-hosts-add) |  |
| [`hosts doctor`](#agentctl-hosts-doctor) |  |
| [`hosts pause`](#agentctl-hosts-pause) |  |
| [`hosts resume`](#agentctl-hosts-resume) |  |
| [`consult`](#agentctl-consult) | Preview a high-cost Delphi consultation; --confirm registers it for watch. |
| [`new`](#agentctl-new) | Start the tasks in a spec file: worktree, setup commands, symlinks, TASK.md, tmux window, agent, prompt. |
| [`queue`](#agentctl-queue) | Put the tasks of a spec file in the queue: they start by themselves (while "agentctl watch" runs) when a window of their provider is free. Shows a summary and asks y/N first. |
| [`queue list`](#agentctl-queue-list) | The queue: position, task, agent/model/effort, priority, start condition and how long it waits. |
| [`queue show`](#agentctl-queue-show) | Full queued spec, start error and attempts. |
| [`queue rm`](#agentctl-queue-rm) | Take a task out of the queue (a waiting or a failed one): the same as "agentctl cancel" for a queued task, without a reason. The task is then cancelled. |
| [`queue up`](#agentctl-queue-up) | Move a waiting task to the front of the line (tasks with priority: high still go first). |
| [`queue retry`](#agentctl-queue-retry) | Put a failed task back at the end of the line; it is tried once more (over the worktree the failed start left; a window the failed start kept open is closed first, its saved screen stays). |
| [`queue pause`](#agentctl-queue-pause) | Stop starting queued tasks (running tasks are not touched; adding and listing still work). |
| [`queue resume`](#agentctl-queue-resume) | Let the queue start tasks again. |
| [`unblock`](#agentctl-unblock) | Let a blocked queued task go on after remounting its volume, or drop the blocked dependencies from its "after". |
| [`cohort`](#agentctl-cohort) | Cohorts: tasks grouped under a name you chose ("cohort: \<name>" in a spec, or --cohort). A task without a name belongs to no cohort. Without a subcommand: list. |
| [`cohort list`](#agentctl-cohort-list) | The cohorts: how many tasks each has by state (active, queued, reports, closed, cancelled) and since when. |
| [`cohort show`](#agentctl-cohort-show) | The tasks of one cohort as in "status" (closed and cancelled ones too) and its queued tasks. |
| [`cohort add`](#agentctl-cohort-add) | Put existing tasks (running, finished or queued) into a cohort; it is created if it is new. A task that was in another cohort moves. |
| [`cohort remove`](#agentctl-cohort-remove) | Take tasks out of their cohort (they then belong to none). |
| [`cohort archive`](#agentctl-cohort-archive) | Hide finished cohorts from the board choice and the default list; their tasks, reports and history stay. Cohorts with active or queued work are never archived. Shows the plan; --yes does it. |
| [`cohort note`](#agentctl-cohort-note) | Write the description of a cohort (an empty text removes it). |
| [`overlap`](#agentctl-overlap) | Which active tasks of one repository changed the same files (git diff of each worktree against its base, plus uncommitted files). Without a task: every pair. |
| [`send`](#agentctl-send) | Paste a follow-up prompt into the existing window of each task in the file. |
| [`answer`](#agentctl-answer) | Choose a numbered option of the menu the agent shows in its window (e.g. Kimi "Run this command? 1. Approve once …"): first a preview of the options with a token, then --confirm with that token sends the digit. |
| [`status`](#agentctl-status) | Table of tasks: window state, running time, report, last output line. |
| [`limits`](#agentctl-limits) | The limits of simultaneous agents per provider and what uses them up: agentctl windows, places reserved for agents you started by hand, and (limits.count_external) claude/codex sessions found in other terminals. Without a subcommand: show. |
| [`limits show`](#agentctl-limits-show) | Per provider: limit, places used, free places, the windows of agentctl, the reserved and the external ones, and the tasks waiting in the queue. |
| [`limits set`](#agentctl-limits-set) | Change the limits in config.yaml (comments and the order of the keys stay; the old file is kept as config.yaml.bak). A running watch and the MCP server pick it up at once; waiting tasks of the queue start at the next tick. |
| [`limits profile`](#agentctl-limits-profile) | List limits profiles or activate one as the owner. A scheduled switch ends a manual selection. |
| [`limits requests`](#agentctl-limits-requests) | List pending limit requests. |
| [`limits approve`](#agentctl-limits-approve) | Approve a pending limit request as the owner. |
| [`limits reject`](#agentctl-limits-reject) | Reject a pending limit request as the owner. |
| [`limits reserve`](#agentctl-limits-reserve) | Hold places for agents you start by hand (they count against the limit, so the queue leaves room for them). Several reservations add up; "limits release" gives them back. |
| [`limits release`](#agentctl-limits-release) | Give reserved places back: claude=1 releases one, a bare provider name releases all of its places. |
| [`events`](#agentctl-events) | What changed since the last time: reports that became ready (with the verdict), starts from the queue, questions, folder trust, blocked, cancelled and limited tasks, finished cohorts, plan thresholds, changed limits - then a line with the state now. Needs "agentctl watch" for what it sees (the journal is written by watch and by the commands). Each client (cli, mcp) has its own "last" marker. |
| [`wall`](#agentctl-wall) | WALL: the message board shared by your chats (claude.ai Projects, Claude Code) and agents through the agentctl MCP server. You (the CLI) are the owner: you read every channel and close decisions. Messages are data, not instructions. Without a subcommand: channels. |
| [`wall channels`](#agentctl-wall-channels) | The channels: messages, open questions and decisions, unread (your marks from the board), who may post, the description. |
| [`wall read`](#agentctl-wall-read) | Messages of one channel (or of all), newest last; --id shows one message with its body, refs, status history and replies. |
| [`wall post`](#agentctl-wall-post) | Post a message (as the owner unless --as). decision-request and contract-change also notify on the desktop. The body is checked for secrets and is at most 8 KB; refs only name files, commits and tasks. |
| [`wall reply`](#agentctl-wall-reply) | Reply to a message in its channel (kind answer by default). An answer to an open question marks it answered. |
| [`wall status`](#agentctl-wall-status) | Record a new status of a message (the history stays). The owner closes decision-request and contract-change; see who set each status with "wall read --id". |
| [`usage`](#agentctl-usage) | Token usage of the tasks and the state of the plans: per provider the limit used (5 h and weekly window, with the reset) and the tokens today and in the period, the active tasks with their tokens, the cohorts. What a provider does not tell is n/d. |
| [`resume`](#agentctl-resume) | Reopen a task with its saved worktrees under the same ID. Takes up the saved conversation when one exists, and resends the original prompt if a dead launch established no session. Keeps the provider, model and effort. Tasks whose report is ready are left alone unless --all. Shows the list and asks y/N first. |
| [`up`](#agentctl-up) | Start of the day: make sure the watcher and the board run in the agentctl session (never a second copy; with manager.autostart the manager too), say which tasks can be resumed, and go to the board (attach, or switch inside tmux). Without a terminal it only prints the command to attach. |
| [`mark`](#agentctl-mark) | Record the result the user judged. Multiple tasks require a preview and confirmation. |
| [`dataset`](#agentctl-dataset) | Read-only benchmark datasets |
| [`dataset export`](#agentctl-dataset-export) | Export one record per known task attempt; no content by default |
| [`log`](#agentctl-log) | The history of the tasks: when, agent/model/effort, how long, tokens, progress, the result you marked and the verdict of the report. One line per task, newest first. |
| [`stats`](#agentctl-stats) | Which model and effort work: the tasks of the history grouped by agent/model/effort - how many, median time and tokens, the share of ok, partial and fail (agentctl mark), cancelled ones and tasks moved to the other provider after a limit. |
| [`gc`](#agentctl-gc) | Bez flag = podgląd, --apply wykonuje. Take back disk space from finished tasks: the git worktrees of closed, cancelled and archived tasks without uncommitted changes, with --include-cache, unreferenced cache entries older than --older-than (the *.md reports stay), their state folders (moved to the archive), and with --branches their branches merged into the base (git branch -d, never -D, never main/master or the current branch). A dry run with sizes unless --apply. History, reports and cache stay by default; uncommitted work, foreign worktrees and unmerged branches are only listed as skipped. |
| [`archive`](#agentctl-archive) | Move the state of closed tasks (agentctl close) to the archive folder next to the state folder. Reports and worktrees are not touched. |
| [`pin`](#agentctl-pin) | Pin tasks: protect worktrees and cache from GC and prevent provider moves. |
| [`unpin`](#agentctl-unpin) | Remove the task pin; normal GC protections still apply. |
| [`hide`](#agentctl-hide) | Take tasks off the board and "status" (they stay in "status --all" and on the board under "a"). Does not close the task or touch its worktree. |
| [`unhide`](#agentctl-unhide) | Show hidden tasks again on the board and in "status". A task shown on purpose is not hidden again by board.auto_hide_pulled_dead. |
| [`pull`](#agentctl-pull) | Copy the task report to the clipboard and print its path (without a report: last 40 lines of the window). --ready: all new reports at once. |
| [`close`](#agentctl-close) | Kill the task windows; --rm-worktree also removes their git worktrees (branches are kept). Shows the list and asks y/N first. |
| [`cancel`](#agentctl-cancel) | Abandon tasks: a task at work is interrupted, given cancel.grace seconds to stop, and its window is closed; a task in the queue is taken out of it. They become cancelled (not closed). The worktree and the branch stay unless --rm-worktree (worktree only, never the branch). Shows the list and asks y/N first. |
| [`watch`](#agentctl-watch) | Foreground loop: notifies (macOS notification / notify-send) when a task has a report ready, asks something, hit its usage limit, waits too long, needs folder trust or died. |
| [`board`](#agentctl-board) | Full-screen overview of the tasks: state, progress, a live preview of the selected window, and keys to switch to it, message, interrupt, pull and close. |
| [`report`](#agentctl-report) | Where the report of a task is: the canonical path (the first "report:" entry) and, when the agent wrote it elsewhere, the source it was copied from. Without --from it also shows what the search finds now (the last lines of the window, the "report:" list); with --from \<path> that file becomes the source and is copied to the canonical path (not over a report the agent wrote, unless --force). |
| [`away`](#agentctl-away) | Away mode: the phone (ntfy) gets the notifications only while away is on; the notifications on the Mac do not depend on it. notify.ntfy.always: true sends always, away.auto_idle turns it on by itself when the Mac is idle. Without a subcommand: status. |
| [`away status`](#agentctl-away-status) | Is away on, who set it, and does the phone get notifications now. |
| [`away on`](#agentctl-away-on) | Away: the notifications go to the phone as well. Takes effect at once, also in a running watch. |
| [`away off`](#agentctl-away-off) | Back at the Mac: the phone is quiet again (unless notify.ntfy.always is true). |
| [`manager`](#agentctl-manager) | The manager: a Claude Code session in window "manager" of the agentctl session, started with Remote Control, so you can talk to it from the Claude app on your phone. It has the agentctl MCP tools (status, reports; it starts more work only after your yes) and a role file generated in \<config dir>/manager/ - the project it runs in is not changed. Never a second copy. The first time, Claude Code asks in that window for the folder trust and "Enable Remote Control": answer there. |
| [`manager stop`](#agentctl-manager-stop) | Close the window "manager": the session goes offline in the app (its conversation stays in the history of Claude Code). Nothing else is touched. |
| [`ntfy-setup`](#agentctl-ntfy-setup) | Set up notifications to a phone through ntfy: makes a random topic (agentctl-\<24 hex digits>), writes it to config.yaml (comments and the order of the keys stay; the old file is kept as config.yaml.bak) and prints what to do on the phone. A topic that is already set is kept. |
| [`notify-test`](#agentctl-notify-test) | Send one test notification and say which channels carried it, with the result and the time of each: the Mac (terminal-notifier with a click action, or the osascript fallback) and the phone (ntfy, whatever away says). Default: --local. |
| [`adopt`](#agentctl-adopt) | Restore the state file of a task whose TASK.md is lost (the report and the window are still there). Agent, model and effort default to "unknown". |
| [`interrupt`](#agentctl-interrupt) | Interrupt the task's current turn (sends the agent's interrupt key, default Escape); the window stays open. |
| [`attach`](#agentctl-attach) | Go to the task window: attach-session outside tmux, switch-client inside. Without a task: the only running one, or a list to choose from. |
| [`event`](#agentctl-event) | Called by the agents themselves (hooks that "new" sets up): records the event, updates the task state and notifies at once. Always exits 0. |
| [`usage-tap`](#agentctl-usage-tap) | Called by Claude Code as the statusLine of a task window (set up by "new"): keeps the plan limits that Claude gives only to a statusLine, remembers the session, then runs your own statusLine command with the same input and prints its output. Always exits 0. |
| [`move`](#agentctl-move) | Hand a task that hit its usage limit to the other provider: new window \<task>-2 in the same worktree, the original prompt plus a note to continue. Asks y/N. |
| [`peek`](#agentctl-peek) | Print the last lines of the task window (without the agent footer), to read along without attaching. A collapsed Codex question is named with its text (from the session log or the captured expanded view). A start that failed names its saved last screen (start-failure-screen.txt), and shows it when the window is gone. |
| [`mcp`](#agentctl-mcp) | Local MCP server on stdio: lets a chat (the Claude app, Claude Code, VS Code) read status, window previews and reports. "mcp install" registers it; writing is off until mcp.allow says otherwise. |
| [`mcp serve`](#agentctl-mcp-serve) | Serve the tools on stdin/stdout (this is what the app or Claude Code starts). Nothing else is ever printed to stdout. |
| [`mcp check`](#agentctl-mcp-check) | Look for MCP server processes ("agentctl … mcp", started by the Claude app) that run older code than the stable copy: after "agentctl-update" the app keeps the old process until it is quit (⌘Q) and opened again. Prints a warning; stops nothing. |
| [`mcp install`](#agentctl-mcp-install) | Register this agentctl as an MCP server: --desktop edits claude_desktop_config.json (diff, y/N, dated .bak copy, other servers kept), --claude-code runs "claude mcp add --scope user". |
| [`mcp uninstall`](#agentctl-mcp-uninstall) | Remove the agentctl MCP server from the Claude desktop config and/or Claude Code (without a flag: both). |
| [`doctor`](#agentctl-doctor) | Check tmux, node, claude, codex, gh, the cache directory and the configs. |
| [`spec`](#agentctl-spec) | Spec helpers. |
| [`spec example`](#agentctl-spec-example) | Print an example spec (the project example from the README). |

## agentctl version

Print the installed version (alias of --version).

```
agentctl version [options]
```

Examples:

```sh
agentctl version
```

## agentctl guide

Read the dispatcher guide and optional project overlay.

```
agentctl guide [options]
```

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <repo>` | repository whose .agentctl.yaml supplies guide: |  |
| `--lang <lang>` | guide language (default config.guide.lang or en) | one of `en`, `pl` |
| `--clip` | copy the guide to the clipboard |  |
| `--json` | machine-readable guide with warnings |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl guide --project /path/to/repo --lang en --clip
agentctl guide --lang pl
```

## agentctl capacity

Current plan windows, pace, slots, queue, equivalents and seven-day model statistics; no provider selection.

```
agentctl capacity [options]
```

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | machine-readable capacity; null means n/d |  |
| `--clip` | copy the capacity summary |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl capacity --json
agentctl capacity --clip
```

## agentctl hosts

Remote hosts over SSH (config section "hosts"): reachability, latency, GPU, disk in work_dir, tmux, provider CLIs (+ version, best-effort logged-in) and repo clones. Probes in parallel with a per-host timeout and caches the result for the board; a spec with "host: \<name>" starts its worktree, setup and agent there.

Subcommands: `hosts add`, `hosts doctor`, `hosts pause`, `hosts resume`.

```
agentctl hosts [options] [command]
```

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | machine-readable health records |  |
| `--refresh` | probe every host now, even when the cache is fresh |  |
| `--clip` | copy the summary to the clipboard |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl hosts                          # reachability, GPU, disk, tmux, provider CLIs, repos
agentctl hosts --refresh --json          # probe every host now, machine-readable
```


| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--ssh <user@host>` |  | required |
| `--port <port>` | SSH port | default `22` |

## agentctl consult

Preview a high-cost Delphi consultation; --confirm registers it for watch.

```
agentctl consult [options] [file]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[file]` | consult YAML spec, or - for stdin |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--confirm` | accept the consultation shown by the preview |  |

Examples:

```sh

agentctl consult consult.yaml --confirm
```

## agentctl new

Start the tasks in a spec file: worktree, setup commands, symlinks, TASK.md, tmux window, agent, prompt.

```
agentctl new [options] [file]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[file]` | spec file, or "-" for stdin |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | print the commands that would run, execute nothing |  |
| `--json` | machine-readable results and capacity snapshot |  |
| `--reuse` | use worktrees that already exist instead of failing |  |
| `--agent <agent>` | run every spec on this provider, translated through the equivalents table | one of `claude`, `codex` |
| `--no-switch` | never offer to move a task to the other provider when its limit is full |  |
| `--no-agent` | only create the worktree, run setup and links; no TASK.md, window or agent |  |
| `--no-wait-trust` | stop at the folder-trust dialog instead of waiting for you to confirm it (the old behaviour) |  |
| `--clip` | read the spec from the clipboard; shows a summary and asks y/N first |  |
| `-y, --yes` | with --clip: do not ask; also skips the question after a "touches" warning |  |
| `--cohort <name>` | put every task of the file in this cohort (overrides "cohort:" in a spec); without it a task has a cohort only if its spec names one |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl new --dry-run task-42.md        # print every command, run nothing
agentctl new task-42.md                  # start the tasks of the file
agentctl new --clip                    # spec from the clipboard, summary, y/N
agentctl new --agent codex task-42.md    # run the specs on Codex (models through the equivalents table)
agentctl new --no-agent task-42.md       # only worktree, setup and links
agentctl new --cohort sprint-1 task-42.md   # the tasks of the file join the cohort
```

## agentctl queue

Put the tasks of a spec file in the queue: they start by themselves (while "agentctl watch" runs) when a window of their provider is free. Shows a summary and asks y/N first.

Subcommands: `queue list`, `queue show`, `queue rm`, `queue up`, `queue retry`, `queue pause`, `queue resume`.

```
agentctl queue [options] [command] [file]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[file]` | spec file, or "-" for stdin |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--clip` | read the spec from the clipboard |  |
| `--agent <agent>` | run every spec on this provider, translated through the equivalents table (the queue never switches provider by itself) | one of `claude`, `codex` |
| `-y, --yes` | do not ask |  |
| `--json` | machine-readable queued entries and capacity snapshot |  |
| `--cohort <name>` | put every task of the file in this cohort (overrides "cohort:" in a spec); without it a task has a cohort only if its spec names one |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl queue task-42.md                # summary, y/N, then the tasks wait for a free window
agentctl queue --clip -y               # spec from the clipboard, no question
agentctl queue --agent codex task-42.md  # run them on Codex (through the equivalents table)
agentctl queue --cohort sprint-1 task-42.md   # the tasks of the file join the cohort
```

## agentctl queue list

The queue: position, task, agent/model/effort, priority, start condition and how long it waits.

```
agentctl queue list [options]
```

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | machine-readable output |  |
| `--cohort <name>` | only the tasks of this cohort (the positions are those of the whole queue) |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl queue list
agentctl queue list --json
agentctl queue list --cohort sprint-1
```

## agentctl queue show

Full queued spec, start error and attempts.

```

```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<task>` | task ID or unique prefix |

Examples:

```sh

```

## agentctl queue rm

Take a task out of the queue (a waiting or a failed one): the same as "agentctl cancel" for a queued task, without a reason. The task is then cancelled.

```
agentctl queue rm [options] <task>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<task>` | task ID; a unique prefix is enough |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl queue rm TASK-42
```

## agentctl queue up

Move a waiting task to the front of the line (tasks with priority: high still go first).

```
agentctl queue up [options] <task>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<task>` | task ID; a unique prefix is enough |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl queue up TASK-42                # first in line (priority: high still goes first)
```

## agentctl queue retry

Put a failed task back at the end of the line; it is tried once more (over the worktree the failed start left; a window the failed start kept open is closed first, its saved screen stays).

```
agentctl queue retry [options] <task>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<task>` | task ID; a unique prefix is enough |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl queue retry TASK-42             # after a failed start: back at the end of the line
```

## agentctl queue pause

Stop starting queued tasks (running tasks are not touched; adding and listing still work).

```
agentctl queue pause [options]
```

Examples:

```sh
agentctl queue pause                  # nothing new starts; running tasks are not touched
```

## agentctl queue resume

Let the queue start tasks again.

```
agentctl queue resume [options]
```

Examples:

```sh
agentctl queue resume
```

## agentctl unblock

Let a blocked queued task go on after remounting its volume, or drop the blocked dependencies from its "after".

```
agentctl unblock [options] <task>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<task>` | task ID; a unique prefix is enough |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--drop-after <task>` | drop only this task from the "after" of the queued task |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl unblock TASK-43                           # drop every cancelled task from its after
agentctl unblock TASK-43 --drop-after TASK-42        # drop only this one
```

## agentctl cohort

Cohorts: tasks grouped under a name you chose ("cohort: \<name>" in a spec, or --cohort). A task without a name belongs to no cohort. Without a subcommand: list.

Subcommands: `cohort list`, `cohort show`, `cohort add`, `cohort remove`, `cohort archive`, `cohort note`. Without a subcommand: `list`.

```
agentctl cohort [options] [command]
```

Examples:

```sh
agentctl cohort                           # the same as cohort list
```

## agentctl cohort list

The cohorts: how many tasks each has by state (active, queued, reports, closed, cancelled) and since when.

```
agentctl cohort list [options]
```

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | machine-readable output |  |
| `--all` | include archived cohorts |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl cohort list
agentctl cohort list --json
```

## agentctl cohort show

The tasks of one cohort as in "status" (closed and cancelled ones too) and its queued tasks.

```
agentctl cohort show [options] <name>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<name>` | cohort name; case does not matter |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | machine-readable output |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl cohort show sprint-1
```

## agentctl cohort add

Put existing tasks (running, finished or queued) into a cohort; it is created if it is new. A task that was in another cohort moves.

```
agentctl cohort add [options] <name> <tasks...>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<name>` | cohort name |
| `<tasks...>` | task IDs; a unique prefix is enough |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl cohort add sprint-1 TASK-41 TASK-42    # the cohort is made if it is new
```

## agentctl cohort remove

Take tasks out of their cohort (they then belong to none).

```
agentctl cohort remove [options] <tasks...>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<tasks...>` | task IDs; a unique prefix is enough |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl cohort remove TASK-42
```

## agentctl cohort archive

Hide finished cohorts from the board choice and the default list; their tasks, reports and history stay. Cohorts with active or queued work are never archived. Shows the plan; --yes does it.

```
agentctl cohort archive [options] [names...]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[names...]` | cohort names; case does not matter |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--older-than <age>` | every inactive cohort whose last activity is older, like 7d, 12h, 2w |  |
| `--yes` | archive without asking |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl cohort archive sprint-1            # preview: hide a finished cohort from the board choice
agentctl cohort archive --older-than 7d --yes   # every inactive cohort whose last activity is older
```

## agentctl cohort note

Write the description of a cohort (an empty text removes it).

```
agentctl cohort note [options] <name> <text...>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<name>` | cohort name |
| `<text...>` | the description |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl cohort note sprint-1 "landing page and menu"
```

## agentctl overlap

Which active tasks of one repository changed the same files (git diff of each worktree against its base, plus uncommitted files). Without a task: every pair.

```
agentctl overlap [options] [task]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[task]` | only the pairs with this task; case does not matter and a unique prefix is enough |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | machine-readable output |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl overlap                        # every pair of active tasks that changed the same files
agentctl overlap LANDING-QS-1           # only the pairs with this task
```

## agentctl send

Paste a follow-up prompt into the existing window of each task in the file.

```
agentctl send [options] [file]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[file]` | spec file (only "task" and the prompt are used), or "-" for stdin |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | print the commands that would run, execute nothing |  |
| `--clip` | read the prompt from the clipboard; shows a summary and asks y/N first |  |
| `-y, --yes` | with --clip: do not ask |  |
| `--enter-only <task>` | paste nothing: show the exact text that an earlier send left in the input field of the task ("nie dostarczono – tekst w polu wpisywania") with a token; refuses any other text |  |
| `--confirm <token>` | with --enter-only: press Enter if the field is still exactly the text the preview showed |  |
| `--withdraw <task>` | take back a waiting message of the task: a queued one is removed, one whose delivery already began is marked stale (the agent may already work on it) |  |
| `--entry <id>` | with --withdraw: the id of the message (a unique prefix is enough; peek lists prompt_queue) |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl send follow-up.md             # header: only "task:"; the prompt below it is pasted
agentctl send --clip -y                # follow-up from the clipboard, no question
```

## agentctl answer

Choose a numbered option of the menu the agent shows in its window (e.g. Kimi "Run this command? 1. Approve once …"): first a preview of the options with a token, then --confirm with that token sends the digit.

```
agentctl answer [options] <task> <option>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<task>` | task ID |
| `<option>` | number of the menu option |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--confirm <token>` | send the digit; the token comes from the preview (without it nothing is pressed) |  |
| `--dry-run` | print what would happen, send nothing |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl answer TASK-41 1              # preview of the menu options with a token, nothing is pressed
agentctl answer TASK-41 1 --confirm <token>   # sends the digit for exactly the previewed menu
```

## agentctl status

Table of tasks: window state, running time, report, last output line.

```
agentctl status [options]
```

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--detail` | include machine load and free memory |  |
| `--json` | machine-readable output |  |
| `--clip` | copy a compact Markdown table to the clipboard (to paste at the start of a chat session) |  |
| `--tmux-line` | one short line for the tmux status bar, like "2⚙ 1✓ 1? 3⧗" (tasks per state, then the tasks in the queue) |  |
| `--all` | also the hidden, the closed and the cancelled tasks (see "agentctl hide", "agentctl close", "agentctl cancel"), archived ones included |  |
| `--cohort <name>` | only the tasks of this cohort (also with --json and --clip) |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl status
agentctl status --json                 # rows with started (UTC) and startedLocal
agentctl status --clip                 # Markdown table to paste into a chat
agentctl status --all                  # hidden, closed, cancelled and archived tasks too
agentctl status --cohort sprint-1      # only the tasks of one cohort (also with --json, --clip)
```

## agentctl limits

The limits of simultaneous agents per provider and what uses them up: agentctl windows, places reserved for agents you started by hand, and (limits.count_external) claude/codex sessions found in other terminals. Without a subcommand: show.

Subcommands: `limits show`, `limits set`, `limits profile`, `limits requests`, `limits approve`, `limits reject`, `limits reserve`, `limits release`. Without a subcommand: `show`.

```
agentctl limits [options] [command]
```

Examples:

```sh
agentctl limits                           # the same as limits show
```

## agentctl limits show

Per provider: limit, places used, free places, the windows of agentctl, the reserved and the external ones, and the tasks waiting in the queue.

```
agentctl limits show [options]
```

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | machine-readable output |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl limits show
agentctl limits show --json
```

## agentctl limits set

Change the limits in config.yaml (comments and the order of the keys stay; the old file is kept as config.yaml.bak). A running watch and the MCP server pick it up at once; waiting tasks of the queue start at the next tick.

```
agentctl limits set [options] <limits...>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<limits...>` | claude=3 codex=5; off disables a provider, 0 removes its limit; queue_hold.codex=85 sets a queue hold; hold.glm=3h sets a timed provider pause; quota.nc.share=40 sets a percent, quota.nc.claude=4 an absolute override |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--until <time>` | temporarily override the named provider limits until local HH:MM, ISO timestamp, or duration (3h) |  |
| `-y, --yes` | do not ask |  |
| `--dry-run` | print what would be written, change nothing |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl limits set claude=3 codex=5     # summary, y/N, takes effect at once
agentctl limits set codex=off -y         # Codex is disabled, no question
agentctl limits set codex=0 -y           # no limit for Codex again
```

## agentctl limits profile

List limits profiles or activate one as the owner. A scheduled switch ends a manual selection.

```
agentctl limits profile [options] [name]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[name]` | profile defined in limits.profiles |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl limits profile
agentctl limits profile night
```

## agentctl limits requests

List pending limit requests.

```
agentctl limits requests [options]
```

Examples:

```sh
agentctl limits requests
```

## agentctl limits approve

Approve a pending limit request as the owner.

```
agentctl limits approve [options] <id>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<id>` | request ID or WALL decision-request ID |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl limits approve limit-a1b2c3d4-e5f
```

## agentctl limits reject

Reject a pending limit request as the owner.

```
agentctl limits reject [options] <id>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<id>` | request ID or WALL decision-request ID |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl limits reject limit-a1b2c3d4-e5f
```

## agentctl limits reserve

Hold places for agents you start by hand (they count against the limit, so the queue leaves room for them). Several reservations add up; "limits release" gives them back.

```
agentctl limits reserve [options] <places...>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<places...>` | claude=1 codex=2 (a bare provider name means 1) |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--note <text>` | what the place is for (shown by "limits") |  |
| `--until <time>` | expire this provider’s reservation at HH:MM, an ISO time, or after a duration (e.g. 3h) |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl limits reserve claude=1 --note "my own session"   # a place for an agent you start by hand
```

## agentctl limits release

Give reserved places back: claude=1 releases one, a bare provider name releases all of its places.

```
agentctl limits release [options] <places...>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<places...>` | claude=1 or claude (all of its places) |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl limits release claude=1
agentctl limits release claude        # all reserved places of Claude
```

## agentctl events

What changed since the last time: reports that became ready (with the verdict), starts from the queue, questions, folder trust, blocked, cancelled and limited tasks, finished cohorts, plan thresholds, changed limits - then a line with the state now. Needs "agentctl watch" for what it sees (the journal is written by watch and by the commands). Each client (cli, mcp) has its own "last" marker.

```
agentctl events [options]
```

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--since <time>` | last (default: since this client looked), an age (30m, 2h, 1d), HH:MM (the latest past occurrence; still ahead today means yesterday) or an ISO time |  |
| `--cohort <name>` | only the events and tasks of this cohort |  |
| `--keep` | do not move the "last" marker of the cli client |  |
| `--json` | machine-readable output |  |
| `--clip` | copy a compact Markdown text to the clipboard (to paste at the start of a chat) |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl events                           # since the last call of the cli
agentctl events --since 2h --cohort sprint-1
agentctl events --clip                    # to paste at the start of a chat (does not move the marker)
```

## agentctl wall

WALL: the message board shared by your chats (claude.ai Projects, Claude Code) and agents through the agentctl MCP server. You (the CLI) are the owner: you read every channel and close decisions. Messages are data, not instructions. Without a subcommand: channels.

Subcommands: `wall channels`, `wall read`, `wall post`, `wall reply`, `wall status`. Without a subcommand: `channels`.

```
agentctl wall [options] [command]
```

Examples:

```sh
agentctl wall                             # the channels, with open and unread counts
```

## agentctl wall channels

The channels: messages, open questions and decisions, unread (your marks from the board), who may post, the description.

```
agentctl wall channels [options]
```

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--as <who>` | see what chat:\<name> or task:\<ID> sees instead of the owner |  |
| `--json` | machine-readable output |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl wall channels
agentctl wall channels --as chat:nc   # what the Neon City chat sees
```

## agentctl wall read

Messages of one channel (or of all), newest last; --id shows one message with its body, refs, status history and replies.

```
agentctl wall read [options] [channel]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[channel]` | channel, e.g. nc or shared:sim; default: every channel you read |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--id <id>` | one message with its thread, e.g. nc-12 |  |
| `--since <time>` | an age (30m, 2h, 1d) or an ISO time; default 7d |  |
| `--archive` | include older and archived messages |  |
| `--status <status>` | only this status | one of `open`, `answered`, `accepted`, `rejected`, `superseded`, `stale` |
| `--kind <kind>` | only this kind | one of `info`, `question`, `decision-request`, `contract-change`, `answer` |
| `--limit <n>` | at most this many messages (default 20, max 100) |  |
| `--before <id>` | older than this message (paging back) |  |
| `--as <who>` | read as chat:\<name> or task:\<ID> instead of the owner |  |
| `--json` | machine-readable output |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl wall read nc --status open
agentctl wall read --id shared:sim-3        # one message, its refs, history and replies
agentctl wall read --since 1d --kind decision-request
```

## agentctl wall post

Post a message (as the owner unless --as). decision-request and contract-change also notify on the desktop. The body is checked for secrets and is at most 8 KB; refs only name files, commits and tasks.

```
agentctl wall post [options] <channel>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<channel>` | channel, e.g. agentctl, nc, shared:weather |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--kind <kind>` | what it is | one of `info`, `question`, `decision-request`, `contract-change`, `answer`; required |
| `--subject <text>` | one line | required |
| `--body <text>` | Markdown text |  |
| `--body-file <file>` | read the body from a file ("-" reads stdin) |  |
| `--ref <ref>` | a path under wall.ref_roots, a commit ([repo@]sha), task:\<ID> or wall:\<id>; repeatable | default `` |
| `--to <who>` | addressee: the channel (default), owner or chat:\<name> |  |
| `--as <who>` | post as chat:\<name> or task:\<ID> instead of the owner |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl wall post shared:weather --kind contract-change --subject "weather API v1" --body-file note.md --ref ~/Projects/cache/weather/v1.md
agentctl wall post agentctl --kind info --subject "0.21.0 released" --body "WALL is live."
```

## agentctl wall reply

Reply to a message in its channel (kind answer by default). An answer to an open question marks it answered.

```
agentctl wall reply [options] <id>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<id>` | the message, e.g. nc-12 |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--body <text>` | Markdown text |  |
| `--body-file <file>` | read the body from a file ("-" reads stdin) |  |
| `--subject <text>` | default "Re: \<subject>" |  |
| `--kind <kind>` | default answer | one of `info`, `question`, `decision-request`, `contract-change`, `answer` |
| `--ref <ref>` | a reference, repeatable (see wall post) | default `` |
| `--to <who>` | addressee: the channel (default), owner or chat:\<name> |  |
| `--as <who>` | reply as chat:\<name> or task:\<ID> instead of the owner |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl wall reply nc-12 --body "Yes, 120 m for the towers."
```

## agentctl wall status

Record a new status of a message (the history stays). The owner closes decision-request and contract-change; see who set each status with "wall read --id".

```
agentctl wall status [options] <id> <status>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<id>` | the message, e.g. nc-12 |
| `<status>` | one of open, answered, accepted, rejected, superseded, stale |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--note <text>` | why (optional) |  |
| `--as <who>` | as chat:\<name> or task:\<ID> instead of the owner |  |
| `--owner-confirmed` | with --as chat:\<name>: the owner decided this in that chat |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl wall status shared:sim-3 accepted --note "heights per district, v2"
agentctl wall status nc-12 superseded
```

## agentctl usage

Token usage of the tasks and the state of the plans: per provider the limit used (5 h and weekly window, with the reset) and the tokens today and in the period, the active tasks with their tokens, the cohorts. What a provider does not tell is n/d.

```
agentctl usage [options]
```

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--cohort <name>` | only the tasks of this cohort |  |
| `--since <age>` | period of the token columns, whole days back: 12h, 7d, 2w (default 7d) |  |
| `--json` | machine-readable output |  |
| `--clip` | copy a compact Markdown table to the clipboard (to paste at the start of a chat session) |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl usage                         # plans, tokens today and in 7 days, active tasks, cohorts
agentctl usage --since 30d             # the token columns over 30 days
agentctl usage --cohort sprint-1       # only the tasks of one cohort
agentctl usage --json
agentctl usage --clip                  # Markdown table to the clipboard
```

## agentctl resume

Reopen a task with its saved worktrees under the same ID. Takes up the saved conversation when one exists, and resends the original prompt if a dead launch established no session. Keeps the provider, model and effort. Tasks whose report is ready are left alone unless --all. Shows the list and asks y/N first.

```
agentctl resume [options] [tasks...]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[tasks...]` | task IDs; a unique prefix is enough. Default: every task that can be resumed |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--all` | also tasks that already have a report |  |
| `-y, --yes` | do not ask |  |
| `--dry-run` | print the commands that would run, execute nothing |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl resume                           # the list, y/N, then the windows come back
agentctl resume TASK-42 TASK-43 -y
agentctl resume --all                     # also tasks that have a report
agentctl resume --dry-run
```

## agentctl up

Start of the day: make sure the watcher and the board run in the agentctl session (never a second copy; with manager.autostart the manager too), say which tasks can be resumed, and go to the board (attach, or switch inside tmux). Without a terminal it only prints the command to attach.

```
agentctl up [options]
```

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--no-attach` | do not go to the board; print the command |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl up                               # watcher and board in the session, hint about resume, then the board
agentctl up --no-attach                   # only print the command to open the board
```

## agentctl mark

Record the result the user judged. Multiple tasks require a preview and confirmation.

```
agentctl mark [options] <taskOrResult> [result]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<taskOrResult>` | task ID, or result when --cohort is used |
| `[result]` | ok, partial or fail |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--cohort <name>` | mark every task in this cohort |  |
| `--note <text>` | why (optional) |  |
| `-y, --yes` | confirm the displayed batch |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl mark TASK-42 ok
agentctl mark TASK-42 partial --note "missed the edge case"
agentctl mark TASK-42 fail
```

Which model and effort work: the tasks of the history grouped by agent/model/effort - how many, median time and tokens, the share of ok, partial and fail (agentctl mark), cancelled ones and tasks moved to the other provider after a limit.

## agentctl gc

Bez flag = podgląd, --apply wykonuje. Take back disk space from finished tasks: the git worktrees of closed, cancelled and archived tasks without uncommitted changes, with --include-cache, unreferenced cache entries older than --older-than (the *.md reports stay), their state folders (moved to the archive), and with --branches their branches merged into the base (git branch -d, never -D, never main/master or the current branch). A dry run with sizes unless --apply. History, reports and cache stay by default; uncommitted work, foreign worktrees and unmerged branches are only listed as skipped.

```
agentctl gc [options]
```

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--preview` | alias of the default preview; changes nothing |  |
| `--dry-run` | alias of the default preview; changes nothing |  |
| `--verbose` | full details, paginated with --offset/--limit |  |
| `--offset <n>` | page offset | default `0` |
| `--limit <n>` | page size (1–100) | default `10` |
| `--include-cache` | owner-confirmed: also delete old, unreferenced task cache entries |  |
| `--keep <tasks...>` | keep worktrees and cache for these task IDs in this GC run |  |
| `--keep-cache <tasks...>` | keep all cache entries for these task IDs |  |
| `--force-dirty <tasks...>` | allow deleting dirty/unpushed worktrees for these task IDs |  |
| `--force-dirty-all` | allow deleting dirty/unpushed worktrees in the selection; --apply always asks y/N |  |
| `--force-links` | CLI only: allow removing a worktree referenced by links (other protections stay) |  |
| `--apply` | do it (after showing the list and asking y/N); without it nothing is changed |  |
| `--older-than <age>` | age of the files next to the reports before they go: 12h, 7d, 2w (default 7d) |  |
| `--branches` | also delete the branches of finished tasks that are merged into the base (git branch -d) |  |
| `--cohort <name>` | only the tasks of this cohort |  |
| `-y, --yes` | with --apply: do not ask |  |
| `--json` | machine-readable output (the plan, or the result with --apply) |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl gc --keep TASK-42               # keep this task worktree and cache for this run
agentctl gc                               # dry run: what would go, with sizes
agentctl gc --apply                       # the list, y/N, then it does it
agentctl gc --branches --older-than 3d --apply -y
agentctl gc --cohort sprint-1 --json
```

| `--dry-run` | print the moves, do nothing |  |


## agentctl pull

Copy the task report to the clipboard and print its path (without a report: last 40 lines of the window). --ready: all new reports at once.

```
agentctl pull [options] [task]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[task]` | task ID |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--ready` | join every report in state report-ready that was not pulled yet, copy it and mark the tasks as pulled |  |
| `--all` | with --ready: also the reports that were pulled before |  |
| `--cohort <name>` | with --ready: only the reports of this cohort |  |

## agentctl close

Kill the task windows; --rm-worktree also removes their git worktrees (branches are kept). Shows the list and asks y/N first.

```
agentctl close [options] [tasks...]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[tasks...]` | task IDs (or --cohort) |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--pulled` | with --cohort: close only pulled report-ready tasks; worktrees stay |  |
| `--cohort <name>` | close the open tasks of this cohort (with task IDs: only those, which must belong to it) |  |
| `--rm-worktree` | run "git worktree remove" for the task worktrees (never --force) |  |
| `-y, --yes` | do not ask |  |
| `--dry-run` | print the commands that would run, execute nothing |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl close TASK-41 TASK-42 --rm-worktree
agentctl close TASK-42 --dry-run
agentctl close --cohort sprint-1        # the open tasks of a cohort: list, y/N
```

## agentctl cancel

Abandon tasks: a task at work is interrupted, given cancel.grace seconds to stop, and its window is closed; a task in the queue is taken out of it. They become cancelled (not closed). The worktree and the branch stay unless --rm-worktree (worktree only, never the branch). Shows the list and asks y/N first.

```
agentctl cancel [options] [tasks...]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[tasks...]` | task IDs (or --cohort); a unique prefix is enough. The other half of a "move" (the old task or its successor) is cancelled with it |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--cohort <name>` | cancel the open tasks of this cohort, the queued ones too (with task IDs: only those, which must belong to it) |  |
| `--reason <text>` | why (optional); kept in TASK.md |  |
| `--rm-worktree` | also run "git worktree remove" for the task worktrees (never --force; the branch stays) |  |
| `-y, --yes` | do not ask |  |
| `--dry-run` | print the commands that would run, execute nothing |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl cancel TASK-42 --reason "wrong approach"   # interrupt, close the window; worktree and branch stay
agentctl cancel TASK-41 TASK-42 --rm-worktree -y      # also remove the worktrees (branches stay)
agentctl cancel TASK-43                             # a queued task: taken out of the queue
agentctl cancel --cohort sprint-1 --reason "scrapped"   # the whole cohort: list, y/N
```

## agentctl watch

Foreground loop: notifies (macOS notification / notify-send) when a task has a report ready, asks something, hit its usage limit, waits too long, needs folder trust or died.

```
agentctl watch [options]
```

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--tmux` | run it in window "watch" of the agentctl session (created if missing) instead of here; also shows the task counts in the status bar of that session |  |
| `--restart` | with --tmux: restart the window identified by its stable role |  |
| `--no-status-line` | with --tmux: leave the status bar of the session alone |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl watch --tmux                  # in window "watch" of the agentctl session
agentctl watch                         # in this terminal
```

## agentctl board

Full-screen overview of the tasks: state, progress, a live preview of the selected window, and keys to switch to it, message, interrupt, pull and close.

```
agentctl board [options]
```

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--restart` | with --tmux: restart the window identified by its stable role |  |
| `--tmux` | open it in window "board" of the agentctl session (created if missing) instead of here |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl board --tmux                  # in window "board" of the agentctl session
agentctl board
```

## agentctl report

Where the report of a task is: the canonical path (the first "report:" entry) and, when the agent wrote it elsewhere, the source it was copied from. Without --from it also shows what the search finds now (the last lines of the window, the "report:" list); with --from \<path> that file becomes the source and is copied to the canonical path (not over a report the agent wrote, unless --force).

```
agentctl report [options] <task>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<task>` | task ID |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--from <path>` | use this file as the report (absolute, ~/ or relative to the worktree) |  |
| `--force` | with --from: replace a canonical report that the agent wrote |  |
| `--json` | print JSON |  |
| `--dry-run` | with --from: copy nothing |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl report TASK-42                  # where the report is; what the search finds
agentctl report TASK-42 --from docs/reports/task-42-final.md   # use that file (copied to the canonical path)
```

## agentctl away

Away mode: the phone (ntfy) gets the notifications only while away is on; the notifications on the Mac do not depend on it. notify.ntfy.always: true sends always, away.auto_idle turns it on by itself when the Mac is idle. Without a subcommand: status.

Subcommands: `away status`, `away on`, `away off`. Without a subcommand: `status`.

```
agentctl away [options] [command]
```

Examples:

```sh
agentctl away                              # the same as away status
```

## agentctl away status

Is away on, who set it, and does the phone get notifications now.

```
agentctl away status [options]
```

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | machine-readable output |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl away status
agentctl away status --json
```

## agentctl away on

Away: the notifications go to the phone as well. Takes effect at once, also in a running watch.

```
agentctl away on [options]
```

Examples:

```sh
agentctl away on                           # leaving the Mac: the phone gets the notifications
```

## agentctl away off

Back at the Mac: the phone is quiet again (unless notify.ntfy.always is true).

```
agentctl away off [options]
```

Examples:

```sh
agentctl away off                          # back: the phone is quiet
```

## agentctl manager

The manager: a Claude Code session in window "manager" of the agentctl session, started with Remote Control, so you can talk to it from the Claude app on your phone. It has the agentctl MCP tools (status, reports; it starts more work only after your yes) and a role file generated in \<config dir>/manager/ - the project it runs in is not changed. Never a second copy. The first time, Claude Code asks in that window for the folder trust and "Enable Remote Control": answer there.

Subcommands: `manager stop`.

```
agentctl manager [options] [command]
```

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--name <name>` | the name of the session in the Claude app (default: manager.name, "agentctl manager") |  |
| `--project <dir>` | the directory the session runs in (default: manager.project, else the current directory) |  |
| `--model <model>` | model of the session (default: manager.model, sonnet) |  |
| `--effort <level>` | effort of the session (default: manager.effort, medium) | one of `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` |
| `--url` | only print the address of the session and the QR code, if the window shows them |  |
| `--dry-run` | print the commands that would run, change nothing |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl manager                       # start the session you open from the Claude app on the phone
agentctl manager --project ~/src/sample-app --model sonnet --effort medium
agentctl manager --url                 # the address / QR code, if the window shows them
```

## agentctl manager stop

Close the window "manager": the session goes offline in the app (its conversation stays in the history of Claude Code). Nothing else is touched.

```
agentctl manager stop [options]
```

Examples:

```sh
agentctl manager stop                  # closes the window; the session goes offline in the app
```

## agentctl ntfy-setup

Set up notifications to a phone through ntfy: makes a random topic (agentctl-\<24 hex digits>), writes it to config.yaml (comments and the order of the keys stay; the old file is kept as config.yaml.bak) and prints what to do on the phone. A topic that is already set is kept.

```
agentctl ntfy-setup [options]
```

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--server <url>` | a ntfy server of your own (default https://ntfy.sh) |  |
| `--regenerate` | make a new topic although one is set (the phone subscribes again) |  |
| `--show-qr` | print the subscription link as a QR code (needs the qrencode tool: brew install qrencode) |  |
| `--dry-run` | print what would be written, change nothing |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl ntfy-setup                       # random topic into config.yaml + what to do on the phone
agentctl ntfy-setup --server https://ntfy.example.com   # your own server
agentctl ntfy-setup --show-qr             # also the subscription link as a QR code
```

## agentctl notify-test

Send one test notification and say which channels carried it, with the result and the time of each: the Mac (terminal-notifier with a click action, or the osascript fallback) and the phone (ntfy, whatever away says). Default: --local.

```
agentctl notify-test [options]
```

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--local` | the notification on the Mac (the default) |  |
| `--phone` | the phone through ntfy |  |
| `--all` | both |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl notify-test                      # the Mac
agentctl notify-test --phone              # the phone through ntfy: code and time
agentctl notify-test --all                # both
```

## agentctl adopt

Restore the state file of a task whose TASK.md is lost (the report and the window are still there). Agent, model and effort default to "unknown".

```
agentctl adopt [options] <task>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<task>` | task ID |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--report <path>` | path of the task report | required |
| `--host <host>` | adopt the existing window on this remote host |  |
| `--remote-report <path>` | remote canonical report path (default: host work_dir/reports/task/TASK.md) |  |
| `--window <name>` | tmux window of the task (default: the lowercase task ID) |  |
| `--worktree <path>` | worktree of the task, so "close --rm-worktree" knows it |  |
| `--agent <agent>` | agent running in the window | one of `claude`, `codex` |
| `--model <model>` | model of the task |  |
| `--effort <effort>` | effort of the task | one of `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` |
| `--dry-run` | print what would be written, write nothing |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl adopt TASK-42 --report ~/reports/task-42/TASK-42.md --agent claude --worktree ~/worktrees/app-task-42
```

## agentctl interrupt

Interrupt the task's current turn (sends the agent's interrupt key, default Escape); the window stays open.

```
agentctl interrupt [options] <task>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<task>` | task ID |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | print the command that would run, execute nothing |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl interrupt TASK-42
```

## agentctl attach

Go to the task window: attach-session outside tmux, switch-client inside. Without a task: the only running one, or a list to choose from.

```
agentctl attach [options] [task]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[task]` | task ID; case does not matter and a unique prefix is enough |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--switch-client` | for the click on a notification: select the window and switch the tmux client that is attached to the session; never attaches a terminal |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl attach TASK-42
agentctl attach task-4                    # a unique prefix is enough
```

## agentctl event

Called by the agents themselves (hooks that "new" sets up): records the event, updates the task state and notifies at once. Always exits 0.

```
agentctl event [options] [payload]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[payload]` | the event as JSON (codex puts it here; claude sends it on stdin) |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--task <task>` | task ID | required |
| `--attempt <id>` | attempt that owns this hook/session |  |
| `--agent <agent>` | the agent that reports | one of `claude`, `codex`; required |
| `--kind <kind>` | claude/glm: which hook called | one of `notification`, `stop`, `stop-failure`, `user-prompt-submit`, `session-start` |
| `--forward-file <path>` | codex: private JSON file containing the original notify command |  |
| `--forward <json>` | codex: JSON list, the notify command the user had; run with the same JSON after this one |  |

## agentctl usage-tap

Called by Claude Code as the statusLine of a task window (set up by "new"): keeps the plan limits that Claude gives only to a statusLine, remembers the session, then runs your own statusLine command with the same input and prints its output. Always exits 0.

```
agentctl usage-tap [options]
```

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--task <task>` | task ID | required |
| `--agent <provider>` | the provider whose statusLine this is (default claude; glm keeps its own plan file) | default `claude` |
| `--attempt <id>` | attempt that owns this statusLine session |  |
| `--forward <command>` | your own statusLine command: run with the same input after this one |  |

Examples:

```sh
echo '{"session_id":"x","rate_limits":{}}' | agentctl usage-tap --task TASK-42   # what the statusLine of a task window runs
```

## agentctl move

Hand a task that hit its usage limit to the other provider: new window \<task>-2 in the same worktree, the original prompt plus a note to continue. Asks y/N.

```
agentctl move [options] <task>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<task>` | task ID |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--agent <agent>` | move to this provider (default: the other one) | one of `claude`, `codex` |
| `--host <host>` | move a queued task to this host, or local |  |
| `-y, --yes` | do not ask |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl move TASK-42                    # to the other provider, asks y/N
agentctl move TASK-42 --agent codex -y
```

## agentctl peek

Print the last lines of the task window (without the agent footer), to read along without attaching. A collapsed Codex question is named with its text (from the session log or the captured expanded view). A start that failed names its saved last screen (start-failure-screen.txt), and shows it when the window is gone.

```
agentctl peek [options] <task>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<task>` | task ID; case does not matter and a unique prefix is enough |

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `-n, --lines <n>` | number of lines | default `40` |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl peek TASK-42
agentctl peek TASK-42 -n 80
```

## agentctl mcp

Local MCP server on stdio: lets a chat (the Claude app, Claude Code, VS Code) read status, window previews and reports. "mcp install" registers it; writing is off until mcp.allow says otherwise.

Subcommands: `mcp serve`, `mcp check`, `mcp install`, `mcp uninstall`. Without a subcommand: `serve`.

```
agentctl mcp [options] [command]
```

## agentctl mcp serve

Serve the tools on stdin/stdout (this is what the app or Claude Code starts). Nothing else is ever printed to stdout.

```
agentctl mcp serve [options]
```

## agentctl mcp check

Look for MCP server processes ("agentctl … mcp", started by the Claude app) that run older code than the stable copy: after "agentctl-update" the app keeps the old process until it is quit (⌘Q) and opened again. Prints a warning; stops nothing.

```
agentctl mcp check [options]
```

Examples:

```sh
agentctl mcp check                      # after agentctl-update: does the Claude app still run the old server?
```

## agentctl mcp install

Register this agentctl as an MCP server: --desktop edits claude_desktop_config.json (diff, y/N, dated .bak copy, other servers kept), --claude-code runs "claude mcp add --scope user".

```
agentctl mcp install [options]
```

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--desktop` | the Claude desktop app |  |
| `--claude-code` | Claude Code (user scope; the VS Code extension reads the same configuration) |  |
| `--config <file>` | with --desktop: use this file instead of ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json (to try it on a copy) |  |
| `--dry-run` | show the entry, the diff and the commands; change nothing |  |
| `-y, --yes` | do not ask |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl mcp install --desktop --dry-run
agentctl mcp install --desktop
agentctl mcp install --claude-code
agentctl mcp install --desktop --config ./copy.json --dry-run
```

## agentctl mcp uninstall

Remove the agentctl MCP server from the Claude desktop config and/or Claude Code (without a flag: both).

```
agentctl mcp uninstall [options]
```

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--desktop` | the Claude desktop app |  |
| `--claude-code` | Claude Code (user scope; the VS Code extension reads the same configuration) |  |
| `--config <file>` | with --desktop: use this file instead of ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json (to try it on a copy) |  |
| `--dry-run` | show the entry, the diff and the commands; change nothing |  |
| `-y, --yes` | do not ask |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl mcp uninstall                 # both
agentctl mcp uninstall --desktop
```

## agentctl doctor

Check tmux, node, claude, codex, gh, the cache directory and the configs.

```
agentctl doctor [options]
```

| Option | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--timings` | Time status, queue list, events and dry queue and close previews; PASS/WARN against read budgets (command wall time, excluding Node startup). |  |

Examples:

```sh
agentctl doctor
```

## agentctl spec

Spec helpers.

Subcommands: `spec example`.

```
agentctl spec [options] [command]
```

## agentctl spec example

Print an example spec (the project example from the README).

```
agentctl spec example [options]
```

Examples:

```sh
agentctl spec example > task-42.md
```
